Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Kitchen, meals & drinks

meal noun

also have a meal, mealtime, before the meal, after the meal

classical

Traupman 72
M-O s.v. meal
Plaut. Trin. 4.2.60; Ter. Eun. 2.3.77: cibum capere (Lewis & Short)

cibus, cibī m.

noun, second declension

food; a meal

Latin has no general word for a meal apart from food: “have a meal” is cibum capere or cibum sūmere, “before the meal” ante cibum. The meals themselves have their names (see breakfast, lunch, dinner).

Other words

  • epulae, epulārum f. pl. — a feast, a banquet

    noun, first declension, plural · also used · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. cibus: syn. epulae

    A rich or festive meal (see banquet).

Examples

  • cibum tibi et familiae cūret utī coctum habeat

    let her see to it that she has food cooked for you and the householdCato Agr. 143.2

  • Ante cibum manūs lavā.

    Wash your hands before the meal.composed

See also food, breakfast, lunch, dinner, banquet.

SourcesLewis & Short: cibus · Lewis & Short: epulae
